title: America's AI power crunch has an unlikely solution: old EV batteries
excerpt: AI is straining America's power grid. One solution: Millions of retired EV batteries could become a low-cost source of energy storage.
content_html:
America's fast-growing fleet of electric vehicles could become an unexpected source of electricity storage as the country races to meet surging power demand from AI.

That's according to Redwood Materials, a startup founded by former Tesla CTO JB Straubel, which now recycles more than 70% of all the batteries in North America.

With millions of EV batteries coming to the end of their lives over the next decade and beyond, Redwood has adapted its business to repurpose many of these batteries to store electricity for the power grid, factories, and AI data centers rather than being immediately recycled.

The proposal comes as electricity demand is rising after years of relatively flat growth. AI data centers, factories coming back to America, and a broader shift toward electrification are putting increasing pressure on the US grid. Redwood cited projections that AI data centers alone could consume 12% of US electricity by 2028.

Meeting that demand has proved difficult because building new transmission lines and other grid infrastructure takes many years. Large battery storage systems can help balance electricity supply and demand while utilities wait for new infrastructure to come online.

Redwood argues that one overlooked source of those batteries is already sitting in American driveways.

More than 6 million electric vehicles have been sold in the US over the past decade. As those vehicles age, many of their battery packs will no longer provide enough driving range for cars, but could still have years of useful life storing electricity.

Redwood estimates roughly 1 terawatt-hour, or 1,000 gigawatt-hours, of used EV battery capacity will become available in the US by 2040. Beginning in the early 2030s, those second-life batteries could supply about half of the country's energy storage demand during that period, the company estimates. And it's aiming to provide about 400 gigawatt-hours of this supply.

The company said it is developing technology that allows battery packs from more than 100 different electric vehicle models to be combined into standardized energy storage systems. Batteries that cannot be safely reused would instead be recycled to recover valuable materials such as lithium, copper, and rare earth minerals.

Redwood said the approach could create lower-cost energy storage while keeping battery materials inside US supply chains.

If successful, the strategy would turn aging EV batteries from a recycling challenge into an energy asset at a time when reliable electricity is becoming one of the biggest constraints on America's AI ambitions.

content_html_zh:
随着美国竞相满足人工智能不断增长的电力需求，美国快速增长的电动汽车车队可能会成为意想不到的电力存储来源。

这是特斯拉前首席技术官 JB Straubel 创立的初创公司 Redwood Materials 的说法，该公司目前回收了北美 70% 以上的电池。

随着数以百万计的电动汽车电池在未来十年及更长时间内即将报废，Redwood 对其业务进行了调整，重新调整其中许多电池的用途，为电网、工厂和人工智能数据中心储存电力，而不是立即回收。

该提议出台之际，电力需求在经历了多年相对平稳的增长后正在上升。 人工智能数据中心、工厂回归美国以及更广泛的电气化转变给美国电网带来了越来越大的压力。 Redwood 援引预测称，到 2028 年，仅人工智能数据中心就可能消耗美国 12% 的电力。

事实证明，满足这一需求很困难，因为建设新的输电线路和其他电网基础设施需要多年时间。 当公用事业公司等待新基础设施上线时，大型电池存储系统可以帮助平衡电力供需。

雷德伍德认为，这些电池的一个被忽视的来源已经存在于美国的车道上。

过去十年，美国已售出超过 600 万辆电动汽车。 随着这些车辆的老化，许多电池组将不再为汽车提供足够的行驶里程，但仍然可以有多年的储存电力的使用寿命。

Redwood 估计，到 2040 年，美国将提供大约 1 太瓦时（即 1,000 吉瓦时）的废旧电动汽车电池容量。 该公司估计，从 2030 年代初开始，这些二次电池可以满足该时期该国约一半的储能需求。 它的目标是提供约 400 吉瓦时的电力。

该公司表示，正在开发技术，允许将 100 多种不同电动汽车型号的电池组组合成标准化的储能系统。 无法安全重复使用的电池将被回收以回收有价值的材料，例如锂、铜和稀土矿物。

雷德伍德表示，这种方法可以创造更低成本的能源存储，同时将电池材料保留在美国供应链内。

如果成功，该战略将把老化的电动汽车电池从回收挑战转变为能源资产，而此时可靠的电力正在成为美国人工智能雄心的最大限制之一。
